thesis: Seagate fell ~10.5% today (to $848.99) on roughly 3.65x average volume, unwinding part of its run from a $209 52-week low (Oct 2025) to a $1,145 52-week high (Jun 18, 2026). This reads as a mechanical correction/profit-taking move rather than a fresh negative catalyst -- there is no company-specific bad news behind today's drop, and the company's most recent quarterly print (non-GAAP EPS ~18% above consensus, revenue ahead of Street) showed no operational deterioration. This still supports a long entry even though the triggering move is purely technical/valuation-driven, because nothing in today's research points to a demand or execution problem at the company -- the risk is that the broader HDD/storage-sector unwind (also hitting Western Digital the same session) continues independent of Seagate's own fundamentals.
invalidation: A confirmed company-specific negative (a guidance cut, an operational miss at the next earnings report, or a new securities/regulatory issue) would invalidate this; a stabilization of the broader storage-sector unwind or a renewed analyst-upgrade cycle would strengthen it.

thesis: Western Digital fell ~8.5% today (to $415.12, a 21.3% decline from its $527.22 close 60 days ago) on ~3.71x average volume, as the memory/storage sector broadly reversed -- Samsung's mid-July preliminary profit report initially lifted the group, but the reaction inverted into a 'sell the news' unwind that has now pulled WDC roughly 35% below its June 18, 2026 52-week high ($799.87), with Seagate and Micron falling in sympathy the same session. invalidation: A confirmed company-specific guidance cut or demand slowdown at WDC's next earnings report, or a structural breakdown in AI-datacenter storage demand, would invalidate this; a stabilization of the sector-wide unwind or renewed analyst upgrades would strengthen it.

thesis: ASML's bull case stays intact: the company raised full-year sales guidance to EUR36-40B (from EUR34-39B), with CFO Roger Dassen calling 2026 'a very strong year,' while the open US Commerce Department inquiry into an alleged unauthorized EUV shipment to China remains an active but unresolved investigation -- Secretary Lutnick has reportedly questioned ASML leadership repeatedly since April 2026, and ASML has firmly denied any violation. This still supports holding even though the company itself now expects China sales to decline significantly in 2026 versus 2024-2025 levels, because that decline is already reflected in the raised guidance range, which the CFO says explicitly accommodates 'potential outcomes of ongoing discussions around export controls' -- i.e., management is guiding through the China falloff rather than being surprised by it. A real pending binary catalyst -- the Oct 14, 2026 Q3 earnings report, 12 days out -- could still move the read before the next review cycle, which caps conviction below high.
invalidation: A confirmed EUV export-control violation finding, a guidance walk-back or demand miss at the Oct 14 print, or an escalation of the Commerce Dept probe to formal enforcement action would invalidate this.

thesis: Thermo Fisher's bull case stays supported: the Q2 2026 print (reported late July) showed revenue accelerating to +10% YoY ($11.99B) and adjusted EPS up 13% to $6.03, both beating consensus, with full-year guidance raised to $47.4-48.1B revenue and $24.93-25.33 adjusted EPS. Today's close ($654.99, roughly flat on the day) sits just ~4.2% below the Sep 30, 2026 52-week high ($683.63). This still supports holding even though the antibody data-integrity controversy remains open -- the company has publicly denied manipulating or fabricating data, attributing flagged discrepancies to presentation-only image adjustments -- because no formal regulatory investigation has opened around it, and the next real test, the Oct 21, 2026 Q3 earnings/guidance print, is still about three weeks out and represents an unresolved binary catalyst that keeps this below high conviction.
invalidation: A guidance cut or organic-growth miss at the Oct 21 print, or a formal regulatory probe opening into the antibody-data allegations, would invalidate this.

thesis: Lumentum continued higher today (to $1,085.42, within a hair of its $1,091.61 all-time/52-week high set this same session, and +39.2% over the past 60 days) as coverage continues to firm up around a draft FCC rule that would ban new-model Chinese optical transceivers from US AI datacenters on national-security grounds, with officials reportedly aiming to finalize it before year-end -- a structural tailwind given Bank of America's estimate that the optical-transceiver market has grown from under $13B (2025) to $26B this year, with high-speed parts running up to 60% short of supply. This still supports holding even though the rule remains a draft that 'could be modified, delayed or abandoned,' and even though the stock's valuation was flagged as stretched in recent coverage (elevated trailing-earnings multiple versus historical norms), because nothing in today's research shows the underlying AI-optics demand story breaking down -- the risk here is a regulatory-catalyst or valuation-multiple compression, not a deterioration in the business itself.
invalidation: A delay, modification, or abandonment of the draft FCC transceiver rule, or a slowdown in AI-datacenter optics orders, would invalidate this; confirmation of the rule as final, or a beat-and-raise quarter validating the current multiple, would strengthen it.

thesis: Carvana's securities-fraud overhang from the January 2026 Gotham City Research report (alleging $1B+ of undisclosed related-party dealings with Garcia-family-controlled DriveTime/Bridgecrest/GoFi) remains open, with multiple law firms (Rosen, Bleichmar Fonti & Auld, Kirby McInerney, Pomerantz, Bragar Eagel & Squire) still soliciting investors nine months on and no dismissal or resolution surfacing in today's research. The stock itself was roughly flat-to-up today (+1.1% to $63.76) with no fresh signal in either direction. This keeps the evidence mixed rather than a clean read -- the unresolved litigation overhang is a real risk, but today's research also surfaced no new negative development (no fresh regulatory action, no confirmed accounting finding) beyond what was already known, so there is no basis to downgrade to exit_existing either.
invalidation: A confirmed adverse finding, an SEC enforcement action, or expanded related-party allegations in the ongoing litigation/investigations would invalidate this hold; a dismissal of the securities claims or continued unit-growth beats at the next earnings report would strengthen it.
